overview: This one-page confidential Navy Department memorandum, dated December 3, 1941, relays intelligence from British Admiralty sources that representatives of two Japanese shipping companies—the Osaka Shoshen Kaisha and Yamashita Steamship Lines—in Montevideo and Buenos Aires had been recalled and were returning to Japan as soon as possible. Received by the State Department on December 5, the document records a potentially significant withdrawal of Japanese maritime personnel from South America only days before the outbreak of war between Japan and the United States.

subfiles.summary: The Office of the Chief of Naval Operations forwards information obtained from British Admiralty sources. Representatives of the Osaka Shoshen Kaisha and Yamashita Steamship Lines stationed in Montevideo and Buenos Aires were reportedly recalled and instructed to return to Japan as early as possible. The confidential memorandum was dated December 3 and received by the State Department on December 5, 1941.

interest: The memorandum captures a small but suggestive movement of Japanese commercial-maritime personnel immediately before the Pacific War began. Its precise timing—four days before the attack on Pearl Harbor—and its reliance on British Admiralty intelligence make it useful for studying Allied monitoring of Japanese shipping networks and possible indicators of impending hostilities. It also documents the presence and withdrawal of Japanese shipping interests in two major South American ports.
